text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- If Macedonia wants to attract foreign investment it needs to show it is a country ruled by law, an editorial says.
- Citizens of Tetovo still have to elect their mayor on January 5. Local elections in Macedonia started on November 17. Citizens hope the "longest" election will finally come to end.
- Traffic on Macedonian-Bulgarian border very slow due to stormy winter weather. Small number of Bulgarian trucks entering Macedonia.
- Macedonian government to discuss on Monday a bill on higher education regulating use of minority languages.

- The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development will participate in construction of gas supply network in Skopje. It granted a 15-year credit of 60 million German marks with a five year grace period for this project. Macedonian private company GAMA gave guarantees for paying the debt back.
